content:
Lean 4 / Mathlib, sorry-free and axiom-clean (only propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound, no native_decide): the Euclidean five-distance theorem g_2 = 5 (Haynes-Marklof) and the sup-norm gap theorem g_inf <= 2^d + 1 (Shutov), with sharpness for d = 2 (= 5) and d = 3 (= 9, Haynes-Ramirez).
https://github.com/ElVec1o/five-distance-sharp
No formalization.yaml, no Challenge.lean comparator set-up. If you don't follow community norms then people aren't going to read your work.
This topic was moved here from #Project announcements > Five-distance and sup-norm gap theorems (formalization) by Kim Morrison.

Fair point... Sorry! I've added both: a formalization.yaml (v0.3) and comparator/Challenge.lean, which restates the headline results in pure Mathlib and proves each from the project, so the file compiling certifies the statements are faithful (supNN_eq is rfl). The sup-norm bound and g_inf(3)=9 are covered; the Euclidean g_2=5 restatement is still to do. Thanks for the nudge toward the norms.
The Challenge.lean is the solution. The challenge file should import mathlib only so people can see exactly what is is you're claiming without having to read your repo at all.

Sorry Kevin. I tried again, I hope I got it right this time: comparator/Challenge.lean (link) now imports only Mathlib with sorry-stubs for both theorems. comparator/Solution.lean (link) imports ThreeGap and closes the sorries from the project's existing results. Both type-check cleanly under lake env lean.
Did you actually run comparator? I don't see any evidence of a script or CI running it.

Thanks Kim, good point. My bad. I just pushed comparator/run.sh which does a 3-step check (Challenge compiles with only sorry warnings, Solution compiles clean, axiom audit passes). Also added a CI workflow so it runs on every push/PR. Latest output is in the README if you want to see it.
